I don't have today's price move data for COP, so I can't tell you what direction the stock moved or by how much. Without that, I can't anchor an explanation to what actually happened.

That said, the backdrop matters: oil prices have been volatile this week around Iran tensions. US crude is trading near $99.60/barrel, and comments from President Trump suggesting the Iran conflict may wind down soon sent Brent crude briefly below $90 earlier in the week—a level it hadn't hit since August. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, lower oil prices typically weigh on earnings and stock performance, since the company's revenue depends directly on what it can sell crude for.
